3rd place @ironman_uk Wales🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿🐉.

Mum, dad, Siënne what happened today. I’m lost for words. I almost did the impossible today. For 5 hours I was in the lead. 

A 22-year-old kid, all alone on Wiseman Bridge, all alone on Heartbreak Hill. I saw it happening. I pushed myself to the absolute limit in this marathon.

Unfortunately, I received a penalty because my sunglasses fell off.
But one thing is certain: I made this race. I fought until the very end.

And thank you to everyone who supported me along the course. Wales, you are absolutely incredible❤️. 

#ironmanwales #imwales #tenby #swimbikerun #ironmantri

a day later, the feeling of disappointment has started to fade. I’ve had a little more time to process everything that happened yesterday✨.

The battlefield of Tenby, literally.

I was in the lead for hours. During the marathon, I could see them getting closer and closer. I gave absolutely everything I had. I went all the way to the limit.

To all the supporters along the course, on Heartbreak Hill, at Wiseman Bridge, in the village of Tenby itself. The young guy with the bucket hat wants to thank you from start to finish, you gave me goosebumps🫶🏼.

Unfortunately, the marathon has the final say.

I’ll be back.

For now, it’s time for a few beers. Cheers Tenby and to all the athletes who conquer the Dragon🐉🍺. 

#ironmanwales #imwales #tenby #ironman #anythingisposible

“TOM CARTER YOU ARE AN IRONMAN” 🐉🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿

Absolute liberation 🙌🏻

4 years after being minutes, even seconds away from losing my life.
Shattered legs in 7 places, double femur fractures including an open fracture, nerve damage, foot drop, over 22kg in weight loss, 4 months in hospital, 6/7 months of being unable to walk, relearning how to walk, relearning how to run, overcoming trauma mentally & physically the list goes on…

Surgeons in Spain did not know whether to operate on me at first, luckily one of them spoke up and said:
“He looks strong we have to try”
I thank my lucky stars that those exceptional surgeons tried & succeeded. 
Fernando Lorente, Maria Jose & Miguel whose surname I don’t know, thank you so much for giving me a second chance at life, I am eternally grateful ❤️

Down but never out.

Nothing is impossible when you truly believe in yourself.

Visualise, action, repeat.

The road will never be easy but it has to be done either way.

The preparation for Ironman has healed me in so many ways, one day I will talk about this at length.

I said to myself:
“This will be the greatest comeback from a major setback”
This is only the start!

15:42:51 is the time to beat, happy but not satisfied!

Ironman Wales see you again in 2028 🐉🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿

From trauma to triumph.

Never give up!

That’s it. I did it. I am an IRONMAN. ☑️

I just swam 2.4miles, biked 112 more and then ran a marathon, all in the rain, on one of the hardest courses in the world at @ironman_uk Wales. 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿🐉 🏊🏻🚴🏻🏃🏻 

I feel absolutely broken, yet completely whole. 🙌🏼

4 years ago, I could barely swim the length of a pool and didn’t like deep water. Whilst at this point, I had some experience of running and biking having done a marathon in 2019 and some sportives but I needed a new challenge and so, I signed up to a local sprint triathlon in 2022 and loved it. From then I did an olympic in 2023 followed by a middle distance in 2024 whilst developing a dream of going the full distance and becoming an ironman. 💭 

However, I was putting it off, taking sabbaticals and seeing the world, until last year, when I decided to make a commitment to myself to make that dream become a reality. 🤝🏼 

And so, over the last 12 months, I swam, I biked and I ran, almost every day, to make it happen, and here I am, an ironman. 💪🏼 

To everyone who supported me along the journey, whether you inspired me, raced with me, trained with me, messaged me, coached me, or just had a 0% beer with me. I couldn’t have done it without you, so thank you. 🙏🏼 

Now pass me a beer! 

#anythingispossible #ironman #IMWales #triathlon

Ironman Wales - 29th

During my 40 hour travel home, I have some time to reflect on the race. And this one hurts.

Throughout my cycling career I dealt with setbacks but I kept coming back determined to succeed. I’ve always seen that persistence as a sign of resilience. However, now with family, continuing to persist with this sport when I continue to fall short feels a bit selfish. 

Frustratingly I was having a really good race with a career best swim, smallest ever gap to the leader of just 3:38, followed by getting to the front of an Ironman for the first time ever after just 65km into the bike. 

Then my front tyre started going soft. That was the beginning of the end. Many tyre plugs, space blankets and cups of tea later with the help of Ironman staff, age groupers, volunteers and spectators I got around the bike course. 

The atmosphere at this race is incredible. After going through the full spectrum of emotions I’m so glad I was able to get around to witness to the packed crowds populating 100% of the run course in the pouring race. 

I had the pleasure of joining the @tenbypengiuns for the week and stopped to chat with them as I we went around the run. I enjoyed that run, I felt like part team and it helped take my mind off my race.

Finishing time 11:41:22

2 years ago vs yesterday 🤯

Yesterday I completed my first ever ultra marathon, raising money for Teddy, a brave 3-year-old boy who’s been battling cancer 💙🧸 There’s still time to donate if anyone wants to support him!

If you’d told me 2 years ago I’d be running an ultra marathon, I’d have laughed in your face 😂

Fast forward 2 years and I’m the fittest I’ve ever been, feeling better than ever and doing things I never thought I’d be capable of. Haven’t touched a drop of alcohol since June either!

It’s mad looking back at how much has changed in just 2 years. Still a long way to go but I’m proud of how far I’ve come 💪

Now looking forward to seeing what the next year brings, with the biggest challenge yet waiting for me… taking on the dragon at Ironman Wales! 🐉🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿

Never thought I’d be saying that 2 years ago 😂

IRONMAN WEEK 3 🏊🏼‍♂️🚴🏻‍♂️🏃🏼‍♂️

A bit of a quieter week in terms of training volume, mainly to recover fully from last weekend’s half marathon.

However, it’s been a pretty productive week in terms of getting more of the kit and equipment sorted that I’m going to need over the next year.

Most importantly, we’ve finally got a bike and she’s a beauty!

Which means I can now start getting some proper outdoor rides in rather than spending all my time indoors. Going to try and make the most of it before the winter weather makes things a bit more difficult 😅

Still plenty of bits to get and lots to learn, but slowly getting everything together.

Anyway, week 3 done. Looking forward to getting back into it properly next week!

Looking back, there are definitely things I’d change from a racing perspective.

But would I actually want to change them?

Probably not.

Wales threw pretty much everything at me, and somehow that made finishing even more rewarding.

Your first Ironman is a pretty special thing. You only get to experience that first finish once.

So prepare as well as you can, control what you can control, and when things go wrong… keep on swimming.

I have started because I wanted to make myself proud! That little boy who always dreamt about greatness! As a kid, I always imagined (for some reason) that 27 years old will be an awesome age for me! Where something big would happen! I was always weak as a kid. I was skinny hence physicality was never my strong point - so I wanted to show this kid that discipline and hard work can create things that once were inconceivable! To go and tell that bitzuk that i ll be doing these distances over 14 hours - i would have never believed it - and that’s the beauty of it💐🥰

When i first started training for an ironman, i couldn’t even swim 2 lengths without stopping- but this never scared me! This motivated me to evolve, because the task was demanding it from me! MEET MATT LUXTON 🏊🏼🚴🏽🏃🏼

📍 From Launceston, Cornwall

❓ Matt loves helping others succeed and achieve their dreams. He does this mainly through his health and fitness coaching. Matt is the owner of Matt Luxton Health & Fitness and the Tamar Performance Centre. Matt’s been involved in triathlon for around 13 years and loves being able to combine coaching other athletes with continuing to train and compete himself.

🥇 Matt has completed more than 50 half-Ironman distance events, and Ironman Wales will be his fifth full Ironman. Matt has qualified for the Ironman 70.3 World Championship three times and has also represented Great Britain in his age group at middle-distance triathlon.

🎯 Matt says.. First and foremost, the goal is to finish! Anything under 12 hours would be a really good day out. Matt would be absolutely chuffed with anything under 11:30. Matt’s peak training weeks happened at the same time as welcoming his son Ollie into the world eight weeks ago, so preparation has involved a little more juggling and a lot less sleep than usual!

Myrtle House wishes Matt the best of luck! We will be rooting  for you 👏🏼📣

IRONMAN WEEK 4 🏊🏼‍♂️🚴🏻‍♂️🏃🏼‍♂️

Week 4 done and that’s the first month of Ironman training in the bag!

Still really enjoying it so far and slowly getting used to fitting everything in alongside CrossFit.

A few takeaways this week:

Swimming drills are a lot harder than I expected. Starting to think this swimming thing is going to take a bit longer to get the hang of than I originally thought 😂

Your hands and feet get ridiculously cold on the bike. Gloves and toe covers have now been bought.

Make sure your cleats are actually screwed in properly before going out for a ride, otherwise you’ll end up losing the bolts during the ride…

Anyway, one month down and still plenty to learn. Looking forward to another month of training!
